raw_response:
I will start from what I did before and make only small changes. On 6.5 mu, I do not like taking big risks. Wheat and maize are my main food and cash support, so I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for chili. I have well water, so I can push fertilizer a bit more steadily than dryland people. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield costs me more, so I would rather not cut too hard on nitrogen. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer and then topdress once around jointing, because wheat here responds clearly if water and fertilizer go together. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, give it heavier nitrogen than wheat, and water at the key stages. For chili, I will not plant too much because it needs more labor and spraying, and some family members work outside, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I will keep chili on 1.5 mu, use improved seed, give it more potassium than grain crops, and manage water and pests closely. Around here, I also watch what other capable growers do. If many people cut fertilizer and the crop turns pale, that is a lesson. I would rather spend a bit more and keep the field standing strong.
